summary.headline: Orchid Pharma Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14% YoY to ₹341 crore and gross margin recovered to about 39%, with EBITDA up 148% to ₹52 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 (post Dhanuka Laboratories merger, comparatives restated on a combined basis) showed revenue of ₹341 crore, up about 14% YoY and 12% QoQ. Gross margin recovered to about 39% from 31% a year earlier, helped by normalisation after last year's inventory write-offs. Reported EBITDA of ₹52 crore absorbed about ₹5 crore of expected credit loss provision and about ₹5 crore of merger-related impairment, both described by management as one-time. Working capital days improved to 218 from 137, and H1 operating cash flow was about ₹118 crore.

segments.name: Anti-microbial stewardship (AMS) platform
segments.commentary: Quarterly EBITDA drag reduced to about ₹1.5 crore. Portfolio is 15 products across 18 SKUs; a new off-patent Pfizer product was added about three months ago. Management says over 120 hospitals are bought regularly, with about 10-15% quarterly growth.

segments.name: Exclusive licensing (explicit/ExplicitF royalties)
segments.commentary: Current royalty and milestone run-rate is about USD 3-4 million a year. Russia 10-year sales estimated at about USD 178 million; first Latin America licence estimated at about USD 80 million over 10 years. UK launch pending under a government-guaranteed procurement model.

segments.name: Sepidro (new product, India launch planned)
segments.commentary: ₹173 crore invested as of 30 Sep 2026. Commissioning targeted by December 2026, validation and initial batches January-March 2027, India launch targeted for Q3 2027 subject to validation, manufacturing licence and clinical trial waiver.

segments.name: 7-ACA (Jammu, 1,000 MTPA)
segments.commentary: Plant designed for 1,000 MTPA with commercial operations scheduled for March 2027. Pilot technology validated; yield improvement continues with an external consultant whose royalty depends on raw material cost gains.

guidance_outlook: Management expects gross margin to be maintained at about 35% through product mix management; it said it does not give formal operating margin guidance.
First merger integration savings (procurement, manufacturing, quality, planning, support) expected to become visible towards end of FY27.
Three to four additional licence agreements hoped for over the next two quarters; these are discussions, not concluded deals. US deal is at a preliminary stage with no timeline.
Middle East and South Africa launches now expected by Q1 2027 after war-related delays.
Recovery is not expected to be a straight line; pricing and demand in core markets remain competitive.
Management said the second half has historically been stronger than the first and it hopes H2 FY27 will be better.
capex_capacity: Sepidro: commissioning by December 2026, validation and initial batches January-March 2027, inauguration January 18, 2027.
7-ACA Jammu: 1,000 MTPA plant, commercial operations March 2027; management said reaching 100% utilisation in two quarters would be wishful thinking.
Capacity rationalisation underway across the Orchid and Dhanuka plants; Dhanuka facility ran at about 80-90% utilisation and Orchid at about 60%.
Cost overrun on the 7-ACA project from commodity price increases over the last six to eight months, to be partly funded by a proposed fundraise.

Board approved a fundraise; uses cited are 7-ACA cost overrun, repayment of Sepidro project debt, and downstream product investment in Chennai (environmental clearance and approvals now in place). No timeline or instrument fixed.
demand_pricing: Injectables showed recovery in the quarter; oral products remain constrained by weak demand and excess industry capacity. Management expects a market consolidation to three players to support pricing.
7-ACA prices have been stable at about USD 50 per kg (plus or minus 10%) over five to six years; no price correction seen recently. Downstream products are only nominal value-add.

Europe demand is weak per management, but complex injectables with little Indian competition support gross margins. Management said it captured some customers after a competitor's import alert, though the benefit was small.
Competitive pricing persists in the core market; one product category had marginal price improvement only.
Management said it cannot disclose geography-wise volumes due to licence confidentiality terms.

qa_highlights.question: Is the one-off adjusted Q2 other income about ₹35 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the analyst's understanding that the adjustment is correct after excluding the two ₹5 crore one-offs.

qa_highlights.question: Other income jumped QoQ and YoY. What drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Two drivers: contribution from the non-cephalosporin business of Dhanuka that merged in, and the sale of older Orchid intangible assets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 7-ACA pricing and yield outlook, and what is the consultant's role?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices are stable at about USD 50/kg plus or minus 10%. The minimum required for commercialisation has been reached and the consultant's royalty incentive is tied to raw-material cost and yield improvement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the PLI benefit and the Jammu GST and tax benefits?
qa_highlights.answer: No clarity on PLI years; the company will seek it after commercialisation. It is entitled to Jammu GST and lower tax-rate benefits, subject to documentation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fundraise rationale and the manufacturing margin on the Sepidro licensing?
qa_highlights.answer: Funds will go to the 7-ACA cost overrun, Sepidro debt repayment and downstream investment. The manufacturing-side PBT margin is about 20-21%; a separate marketing agreement is under negotiation.

qa_highlights.question: Is a US licensing deal close?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The US is at a preliminary stage with no timeline; the three to four announcements refer only to advanced discussions in other markets.

qa_highlights.question: Can Orchid sell Sepidro in India, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: The India commercialisation partner deal is at near-signature stage. Filing with DCGI would follow manufacturing completion by March 2027; at least six months is expected for licensing, with a commercial launch hoped for around September-October 2027.

risks_watch: Gross margin sustainability: management targets about 35%, versus 39% this quarter, and warns margins depend on product mix and competitor price cuts.
Fuel and power costs were about 30% higher YoY due to the Middle East conflict; this remains a cost headwind.
Receivable days rose to 200 from 113, while a ₹5 crore expected credit loss provision was booked; collection progress needs monitoring.
Sepidro and 7-ACA execution: commissioning, validation, regulatory approvals, and cost overruns on 7-ACA.
Licensing pipeline: UK launch timing, Middle East and South Africa delays, and the unconfirmed three to four deals expected in two quarters.
Proposed fundraise has no fixed size, instrument, or timeline; dilution and use of proceeds need tracking.
Oral antibiotic oversupply and pricing pressure in the core business.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the margin recovery and the licensing platform, but cautious on near-term demand and pricing. Management was evasive on the US deal, the fundraise size and timing, and exact margin guidance, and said it does not give short-term guidance as policy.
key_quotes: While Q2 and H1 show an encouraging improvement, it would be premature to expect a straight line recovery.
Our priority now is to convert the gross margin recovery into sustainable operating profitability through tight cost control and higher productivity.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Sepidro India launch targeted Q3 2027 subject to validation, licence and trial waiver, and Middle East and South Africa launches now expected by Q1 2027; the Pfizer off-patent product was added about three months ago.

rows.label: Three to four additional licence agreements
rows.why: Management hopes for 3-4 licence deals in advanced discussions over two quarters, but these are not concluded, and the US deal is preliminary with no timeline; current royalty run-rate is about USD 3-4 million a year.

rows.label: Merger integration savings
rows.why: Procurement, manufacturing, quality and planning savings from the Dhanuka merger are expected to become visible towards end of FY27, after the ₹135 crore H1 other expenses base.

rows.label: Receivable days normalisation

tone.note: Management was confident on the margin recovery, the Sepidro and 7-ACA timelines and the licensing platform, but cautious on near-term demand and pricing and evasive on the US deal, fundraise size and timing.
